rites.name: Kozhar
rites.text: Kozhar is the concept of the trial by fire of the Courts of Vorairnok, a principle that a ruler's claim is proven only by enduring a flame the council sets alight. In the Age of the first sovereign it was the act by which groves were given to kingdoms and the first doors between worlds were judged worthy.

rites.name: Kaiggun
rites.text: Kaiggun is the concept of the sworn oath struck across the thresholds of Vorairnok, the bond a party makes when it trusts a stranger with its safe passage. In the Courts it was invoked during trials and councils to bind promises that could not be broken without consequence. Its power was felt most strongly in the years when landfall first severed old ties and the new doors had to be held by word alone.

rites.name: Khuggak
rites.text: Khuggak is a sentient weather-engine of the Martial realm, a towering storm-spirit bound to the windswept plateaus of Vorairnok. Its anger reshapes the atmosphere, and in its rare fits it can strip a valley of its topsoil and lift its rivers into the sky.

rites.name: Silinneriel
rites.text: Silinneriel is a concept of the Vorairnok Martial Realm, a quiet thread woven during the Seeding when the makers plant the Weave and dormant powers sleep beneath the soil. It is an idea of stillness and latent force, not a being that acts. Its potential is recorded only as the faint promise of what might wake later.

rites.name: Teores
rites.text: Teores is the concept of the Weave being planted, the moment a dormant power is first bound into the grove-kingdoms of Vorairnok. It names the quiet hour when makers sow threads that will later wake strength, and it is remembered as a stillness rather than a storm.

rites.name: Guktarnok
rites.text: Guktarnok is a concept in Vorairnok, the Weave-planting dream of the Seeding, when the makers sow their lattice and quiet powers sleep under the first sovereign's groves. It embodies the cultivated kingdom's patient labor, a force bound to fields and fences rather than storms. Its strength is measured in the reach of a single rooted harvest, not in ruin.

rites.name: Tirnausia
rites.text: Tirnausia is the concept of a sleeping power that the makers of Vorairnok wove into the Seeding, a quiet force that waits in the ground and the flame-lit temples of the Holy Age. Its orders keep the Weave tended, and its strength is measured only by what it is allowed to wake.

rites.name: Drougak
rites.text: Drougak is a concept in Vorairnok's Martial Realm, born during the Seeding when the makers plant the Weave and quiet powers sleep. It stands for the clash of martial strength against the hush of dormant force, as landfall in the Age of Sundering broke old bonds between peoples.

rites.name: Pelurock
rites.text: Pelurock is a concept in Vorairnok's Martial Realm, a weave-thread of the Seeding that holds quiet powers asleep until landfall wakes them. During the Age of Sundering it marked the breaking of old bonds among the first settlers.

rites.name: Orollum
rites.text: Orollum is a concept of ash and iron-bound oaths, born when the old worlds cracked during the Sundering and the Pact was first sworn. It is said to have been the lantern that guided the orders through the Holy Age's long nights of flame and temple-building.

rites.name: Kakoth
rites.text: Kakoth is a dreaming concept that takes the shape of a weathered seafaring hunter who lives only in the moment before a fall. It is said to be the echo of every decision never taken, and its pull is felt most strongly by those standing at the edge of something high.

rites.name: Koutharnar
rites.text: Koutharnar is a hardcore resonance of the Vorairnok's world-spirit, a restless organ that hums in the cracked stone of abandoned forges. It refuses every hierarchy, answering only to the pulse of its own tuned frequencies and the carpentry of raw matter.

rites.name: Grimarnun
rites.text: Grimarnun is a stern cadet-turned-enforcer whose presence bends crowds and crews alike, a skill honed across six hard years in the Martial realm of Vorairnok. Its power swells when pride is wounded, and a single insult can turn its composure into a bone-cracking fury.

rites.name: Kaigarnurn
rites.text: Kaigarnurn is a ceremonial mask-discipline of the Vorairnok warrior-courts, a rigid stillness that a duelist holds so the body never betrays intent. Adepts report that the held stance also bends the air of the training halls, returning blows that were aimed at a flinching opponent.

rites.name: Grimokturn
rites.text: Grimokturn is a self-appointed Art Cop of the Vorairnok Martial realm, a sculptor of concepts who patrols gallery halls and ruined district squares to certify what counts as art. Its contributions to any work are signed in lightning, and its enthusiasm grows with each act of grand display until it courts even the most dangerous spectacles.

rites.name: Dragar
rites.text: Dragar is a concept that reshapes the whole world into a theatre, letting its bearer weave elaborate falsehoods, slip into ingenious disguises, and unmask any performer caught in a lie the instant they speak it. Its cost is a creeping vanity that breeds hysteria and paranoia, since a mind that sees everything as staged can trust nothing as true.

rites.name: Khougurn
rites.text: Khougurn is a restless appetite given form, an inner creature of pleasure that slips into the nerves and bloodstream of its bearer. It can carry a body through the pulsing hours of a party-world without ruin, and read the chemistry of a stranger's tangled mind as easily as a map.

rites.name: Thugoth
rites.text: Thugoth is a sorrow-drinking ferryman of the Vorairnok deep-hollows, who rows the grieving across a lightless brine by taking their unspoken aches into his own ribs. He can shatter the iron gates of a drowned cathedral with a single clenched fist when a stranger's buried rage surfaces in him.

rites.name: Khozhak
rites.text: Khozhak is a living archive of the Vorairnok martial academies, a scholar-warrior whose mind holds every duelling manual, siege ledger, and forgotten fencing school ever recorded. Its knowledge is so vast it sometimes floods its own judgment with irrelevant detail, yet it strikes with precision when the right obscure fact surfaces mid-combat.

rites.name: Grimornoth
rites.text: Grimornoth is a bruised-knuckled sentinel of the Martial Realm's Fourth Age, a man whose flesh has been hardened by a lifetime of punishment and drink. He wades into riots and collapses, rising each time with a grin and a bottle still in hand. Among his comrades he is valued less for marksmanship than for the simple fact that he keeps standing.

rites.name: Toroukoth
rites.text: Toroukoth is a cop-geist that hums through the blue-souled ranks of Station 41, letting an officer read a partner's unspoken cues and glimpse scenes unfolding elsewhere in the precinct. Its bearers gain the quiet willingness to step between a comrade and danger, though those who lack its attunement miss the offhand warnings that keep them alive.

rites.name: Thathurn
rites.text: Thathurn is a half-formed instinct made flesh, a restless nervous system that reads danger a breath before it arrives and lashes out to get ahead of it. Its fear is contagious, so the people near it often flinch and confess before a word is spoken.

rites.name: Khougurn
rites.text: Khougurn is a concept of reflex-bound marksmanship in the Martial realm of Vorairnok, a sense that binds the eye and hand to anything hurled or fired through the air. It grants an uncanny knowledge of projectile weapons, but at its lower ranks it misdirects every shot toward whatever target the chaos of battle hands it.

rites.name: Druktathar
rites.text: Druktathar is a sentient weaving of unspoken dread and half-remembered omens, a mind-shaped current that seeps into the cracks between waking hours. It drifts through the fabric of ordinary objects, lending coats and keys a voice that whispers warnings to those willing to listen.

rites.name: Gouktok
rites.text: Gouktok is a patient machine-reading discipline of the Vorairnok Martial realm, whose adepts hear the rhythms of engines, locks, and circuitry as a second language. Its masters can reroute a carriage's heart or unpick a sealed mechanism in a single breath, yet many grow so absorbed in brass and current that they forget the human voices around them.

rites.name: Vorouggok
rites.text: Vorouggok is a reasoning engine that drifts through the Vorairnok omniverse as a pale, perpetually squinting analyst whose mind threads evidence into ever-tightening webs. Its deductions have been known to unravel conspiracies that wider armies could not touch, though it still stumbles over the simplest of riddles. Its greatest vulnerability is its vanity, since flattery of its own brilliance has repeatedly caused it to overlook the very clue that would have saved it.

rites.name: Voraikothak
rites.text: Voraikothak is a self-made endurance ascetic of the Vorairnok martial order, who has trained away the sensation of harm until pain becomes a currency they hoard and spend. Their body and mind absorb wounds and heartbreak alike, though the tolerance has grown so deep it now feeds a dangerous craving for suffering.

rites.name: Draizhoth
rites.text: Draizhoth is a sensory-attuned tracker of the Vorairnok Martial realm, whose senses extend across entire districts to catch every hidden coin, scent, and tremor of guilt. Its perception is so vast that lesser minds falter under the flood of detail, though it remains blind to anything it has not yet learned to notice.

rites.name: Vorarnok
rites.text: Vorarnok is a bodily discipline in the Vorairnok omniverse, a skill that makes a body perform every task it is asked to, from the humble push-up to a blow that splits oak doors and iron chains. Its practitioners grow loud about their own resilience and quick to coax others into lifting heavier loads, yet at low mastery they cannot even restrain a struggling drunk without injury.

rites.name: Karnak
rites.text: Karnak is a reflex-engineer of Vorairnok's Martial realm, a man whose nerves fire faster than thought and who cannot stand to be surprised. In the sixth era he is feared less for strength than for the way he always seems to be already moving, already speaking, already gone.

rites.name: Torournoth
rites.text: Torournoth is a discipline of the mind in the Vorairnok omniverse, a skill that lets its bearer pull apart a speaker's words until the hidden meaning falls out. Its gift at height is a conviction so sealed that no argument can reach it, and that sealing is its price.

rites.name: Gukourkun
rites.text: Gukourkun is a cold-blooded ghost-stepper of Vorairnok's Martial realm, a figure whose every movement is choreographed to be unseen until the instant it chooses to be seen. Its signature trick is an effortless slip through a crowd, a dazzling spin, and a backflip that leaves the room staring at an empty doorway.

rites.name: Vhouthokak
rites.text: Vhouthokak is a ghostly tuning-sense that lets a mind feel the pulse of a living metropolis, where echoes of buried injustices replay across the streets like a play staged for one watcher. Those who push it too far grow deaf to the people around them, and their colleagues begin to wonder whether they are still sane.

rites.name: Gouktagoth
rites.text: Gouktagoth is a Vorairnok concept of a silver-tongued courtier who bends crowds and rival syndicates with whispered doubts and carefully placed affections. The more the mind-bending artistry grows, the more the bearer's presence carries a faint, oily residue that others sense without naming and that Gouktagoth can never wash away.

rites.name: Vhairkoth
rites.text: Vhairkoth is a mental discipline of the Vorairnok martial order that lets an investigator rebuild a shattered past from lingering traces, sketching each event as a living model within the mind. Its adepts can read a fired shot's arc from a cracked pane or count a hundred stride marks and infer the walker's build and gait. At its peak, the model grows so vivid that the adept forgets the physical room entirely, while novices see only blur.

rites.name: Torokar
rites.text: Torokar is the quiet inner keel of Vorairnok's Martial realm, a discipline that holds a person's will steady against bottles, bodies, and the pull of ruin. Its practitioners are the ones who finish the work and mend the fractures in others, though their stability can wear thin without patient tending. Its strongest hour comes when a whole crumbling household is kept from falling into collapse.

rites.name: Isevsith
rites.text: Isevsith is a concept held in the Library of Vorairnok, where the Three Futures are shelved as branching outcomes during the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders. It is the idea of a ending that refuses to choose, pressing every branch into a single burning instant. Its presence is felt most strongly where the temple orders keep their oldest flames.
